findings.summary: DBS, OCBC and UOB announced that they completed live domestic Singapore-dollar interbank transactions using tokenised deposits on Swift’s blockchain-based ledger. The banks say the work provides insights for round-the-clock interbank payments and may support future corporate treasury, trade and digital-commerce services; it is not a Hong Kong regulatory requirement or a confirmed customer rollout.
findings.title: DBS, OCBC and UOB complete first live tokenised-deposit transactions on Swift’s ledger

rendered_html: 📔 Regulatory Bulletin — 11 September 2026 (Daily) Executive Summary • 🟡 Singapore’s three local banks report their first live interbank tokenised-deposit transactions on Swift’s ledger. This is a medium-impact benchmark for payments-infrastructure and digital-service strategy, not a Hong Kong requirement or product launch. SG/UK/GLOBAL Benchmark Comparable overseas developments and commercial/control benchmarks. They do not establish Hong Kong requirements. 🟡 DBS, OCBC and UOB complete first live tokenised-deposit transactions on Swift’s ledger 🇸🇬 Item ID: item-20260910-hk-banks-news-dbs-swift-ledger ⏰ Deadline: No source deadline stated Products: Payments, Digital banking DBS says that DBS, OCBC and UOB completed live domestic Singapore-dollar interbank transactions using tokenised deposits on Swift’s blockchain-based ledger on 10 September 2026. The banks describe this as the first live interbank use of tokenised deposits by the three Singapore banks and say it provides insights into supporting round-the-clock interbank payments beyond traditional processing windows. They identify corporate treasury, trade and digital commerce as possible future service areas, rather than confirming customer availability. This issuer-controlled market announcement is a comparable payments-infrastructure development for Hong Kong monitoring; it does not establish a Hong Kong obligation, a current control outcome or a source deadline. Source: DBS, OCBC and UOB complete first live blockchain-enabled transactions on Swift’s ledger Watch List • Monitor whether the participating banks disclose customer availability, operating scope, regulatory engagement, resilience evidence or a production-control design for the Swift-ledger use case.
